meta.title: Customization overview
meta.description: The six ways to change React Scheduler, from a CSS variable to a rendering of your own — lightest first.

scope: Six levels, from the lightest to the heaviest. Each one costs more to maintain than the one before it, so take the first that does what you need — and stop there.

variables.text: A value: a color, a radius, a height. Set a token on the component, in your own stylesheet, or through the tokens prop, and everything built from it follows. Nothing about the structure changes. See CSS variables.

classNames.text: A hook for your own CSS. classNames adds a class to any part, next to the library’s own, so your rules can target it without depending on the library’s class names. With unstyled, they are the only classes there are.

slotProps.text: An attribute on a part: a title, a data attribute, an extra class, a ref. The part stays the library’s; you are only adding to its props. A function form receives the owner state, so the value can depend on the item or the shift.

slots.text: The part itself, replaced. Your component receives the props the built-in one would have had — including the ref and the handlers — and renders whatever it likes. See <link to="/customization/slots/">Slots and overrides</link>.

handlers.text: Behavior rather than markup. A middleware runs before the component acts and can change the outcome or cancel it — a confirmation, a permission, an unsaved change. See <link to="/events-and-middleware/">Events and middleware</link>.

hooks.text: The model without the markup. When the structure itself has to be different, take the state and the prop getters and render your own. See <link to="/headless-api/">Headless API</link>.
